https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Identification of esculin as a direct modulator of IGF1 in cervical cancer with integrated computational and experimental studies
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Aberrant activation of the insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) signaling axis plays a central role in tumor proliferation, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Although most therapeutic strategies have focused on inhibition of the IGF1 receptor (IGF1R), direct targeting of the IGF1 ligand remains largely underexplored. An integrated computational-experimental pipeline was employed to identify phytochemicals that directly modulate IGF1. In the computational phase, a library of 75 natural compounds was screened by molecular docking against model 11 of the NMR conformer of IGF1 (PDB ID: 1PMX), followed by ADMET profiling, PASS-based biological activity prediction, and 500-ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations complemented by essential dynamics, free-energy landscape (FEL), and MM-PBSA analyses. In the experimental phase, the top candidates were evaluated using in vitro cytotoxicity assays, ELISA-based IGF1 quantification, and fluorescence spectroscopy with Stern–Volmer analysis. Esculin and rotenone were identified as the top-ranked binders from docking analyses. ADMET profiling indicated more favorable pharmacokinetic and safety characteristics for esculin. PASS predictions supported anticancer and antimetastatic potential for both compounds. Long-timescale MD simulations indicated that esculin altered IGF1 conformational dynamics, as reflected by reduced backbone deviation, controlled residue flexibility, persistent hydrogen-bonding interactions, and confinement within a distinct thermodynamically favorable energy basin compared with apo IGF1 and the rotenone-bound complex; MM-PBSA re-scoring returned comparable total binding free energies for the two complexes. In vitro assays subsequently demonstrated a clear dose-dependent cytotoxic effect of esculin in HeLa cells, whereas rotenone showed minimal antiproliferative effects. Esculin significantly reduced intracellular IGF1 protein levels (p < 0.001) and directly interacted with recombinant IGF1, as indicated by fluorescence quenching. Esculin is identified as a promising natural IGF1-binding compound with modulatory potential, supported by consistent computational and experimental evidence. These findings highlight its potential as a lead compound for the development of IGF1-targeted anticancer therapies.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Symptom management self efficacy relates to self perceived burden and IADL in lung cancer patients with treatment associated pneumonitis
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: To examine symptom management self-efficacy, self-perceived burden, and impairment in instrumental activities of daily living among patients with lung cancer who developed treatment-associated pneumonitis (TAP) after radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy, and to analyze the relationships among these factors. This cross-sectional study included 140 TAP patients from October 2024 to June 2025. Data were collected using the Self-Efficacy for Symptom Management Scale (SESMs), Self-Perceived Burden Scale (SPBS), and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale (IADL). Pearson correlation, group comparisons, and hierarchical regression were performed. Mean SESMs, SPBS, and IADL scores were (6.00 ± 0.38), (34.35 ± 5.00), and (21.04 ± 4.00), respectively. SESMs scores were negatively correlated with SPBS scores (r=-0.663) and IADL scores (r=-0.634) (both P < 0.001); SPBS scores were positively correlated with IADL scores (r = 0.429, P < 0.001). After covariate adjustment, SESMs scores additionally explained 20.5% of the variance in SPBS scores (ΔR² = 0.205) and 17.5% of the variance in IADL scores (ΔR² = 0.175). SPBS and IADL scores jointly explained an additional 21.0% of the variance in SESMs score (ΔR² = 0.210). Among patients with TAP, those with higher symptom management self-efficacy had lower self-perceived burden and less impairment in instrumental activities of daily living.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-0.title: Nanoparticles as carrier and drug
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-0.abstract: A lipid nanoparticle formulation degrades an immunosuppressive receptor on tumour-associated macrophages through its lipids alone, while its messenger RNA cargo reprograms these cells in situ into anti-tumour chimeric antigen receptor macrophages, reshaping the immune microenvironment of malignant ascites in gastrointestinal cancer.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41571-0.title: Emerging strategies for paediatric cancer predisposition: detection, surveillance and prevention
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41571-0.abstract: A substantial proportion of childhood cancers occur in children who are genetically predisposed to develop that cancer. Close surveillance of children with cancer predisposition syndromes enables early cancer detection and results in better survival outcomes and less therapy-related toxicity, although many more predisposition syndromes are likely to exist and remain undetected. Building on conventional clinical surveillance protocols, new approaches are being explored, including liquid biopsy, molecular or metabolic biomarkers, enhanced imaging and microbiome profiling for the purposes of both improved surveillance and the discovery of additional predisposing factors. Knowing the specific genes, expressed proteins and biological pathways associated with a specific cancer predisposition syndrome might permit the use of targeted agents or vaccines, as well as the introduction of lifestyle changes to delay, reduce or even eliminate the development of cancer. Preclinical studies investigating the risks and benefits of preventive interventions would be greatly aided by the identification or development of animal models that faithfully recapitulate human syndromes. The incorporation of artificial intelligence to complement the clinical and experimental assessment of cancer risk based on the syndrome, genotype, modifier genes, family history, environmental exposures and other factors will undoubtedly improve the management and, ultimately, the outcomes of children with an increased genetic risk of cancer. In this Perspective, we discuss strategies to identify new cancer predisposition genes, developing approaches to cancer surveillance, emerging efforts for cancer prevention in high-risk patients, and the role of artificial intelligence in improving data analysis and optimizing medical decision-making. Many childhood cancers occur in children with an underlying predisposition to developing cancer. Thus, identifying individuals with a cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS), ideally before the development of cancer, can enable regular clinical surveillance and potentially the introduction of preventive measures. In this Perspective, the authors describe cancer detection, surveillance and prevention strategies for the management of children with a CPS, as well as the potential of artificial intelligence-based methods to optimize the management of these individuals.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-0.title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-0.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy. Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41584-0.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated inflammatory arthritis
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41584-0.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated inflammatory arthritis (ICI-IA) represents the most common rheumatic immune-related adverse event, characterized by a distinct clonal expansion of CD8+ T cells that often mirrors the immune pathways driving antitumour responses. Clinically, ICI-IA presents with diverse phenotypes, including polyarticular and oligoarticular patterns, and is notably persistent, often continuing as a chronic condition long after the cessation of immunotherapy. Unlike traditional autoimmune arthritis, ICI-IA is predominantly seronegative, making diagnosis reliant on clinical recognition and the exclusion of mimics such as metastatic cancer and other immune-related adverse events. Management strategies prioritize symptom optimization to maintain patient quality of life and facilitate the continuation of life-saving cancer therapy. Treatment includes glucocorticoids and increasing use of conventional and biologic DMARDs. This approach is aimed at minimizing glucocorticoid toxicity while preserving the efficacy of the checkpoint inhibitor therapy, highlighting the need for a balanced, multidisciplinary approach to care. Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated inflammatory arthritis is the most common rheumatic immune-related adverse event. In this Review, the authors discuss current insights into the pathogenesis, clinical presentations and management of immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated inflammatory arthritis, underscoring its distinct biology and therapeutic considerations.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 Alters Extracellular Vesicle Secretion and Cargo Composition in Cellular Models
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and confer the neomorphic production of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D2HG), which drives epigenetic remodeling. Growing evidence suggests this neomorphic activity may also affect how tumor cells communicate; small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are elevated in gliomas, though how mutant IDH1 shapes sEV production and cargo remains poorly understood. Using glioblastoma and chondrosarcoma cell models, we show expression of mutant IDH1 correlates with a trend of increased sEV secretion, and that D2HG is packaged into sEVs that are taken up by cells. Cell-permeable D2HG treatment dose-dependently increased sEV release from IDH1 wild type cells. Untargeted proteomics showed that mutant IDH1 expression remodeled sEV cargo in a cell type-specific fashion, with mutant chondrosarcoma sEVs enriched in one-carbon metabolism enzymes, and mutant glioma sEVs in lysosomal luminal proteins and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperones. Mutant IDH1 glioma cell transcriptomics suggested expanded ER folding capacity and reduced ribosomal pathways, and sEVs from these cells decreased nascent protein synthesis in IDH1 wild type recipient cells. Together, this suggests sEVs can serve as carriers of mutant IDH1 phenotypes.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Background & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: Arrest-associated transcriptional programmes outweigh apoptosis-associated programmes in treatment-naive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is driven by mutant KRAS, and RAS inhibitors now extend survival in previously treated metastatic disease. Whether treatment shrinks a tumour or only halts its growth depends partly on whether cancer cells die or stop dividing, yet how untreated PDAC cells are balanced between these programmes is unknown. Aims: We aimed to characterise the balance between apoptosis-associated and arrest-associated transcriptional programmes in treatment-naive PDAC and to examine their relationships with tumour subtype, TGM2 expression, tissue organisation, survival and drug sensitivity. Methods and results: We scored 52,999 malignant cells from 18 untreated patients in the Hwang atlas using a transcriptional contrast between genes associated with apoptosis and genes associated with resistance to apoptosis or cell-cycle arrest. In every patient the contrast was shifted toward the arrest-associated side: using equality between the two sides as the dividing threshold, 86.3% of cells with an informative score fell on that side, although the proportion depends on the threshold chosen. The shift recurred in the independent Steele atlas (median 71.6% per sample, range 37.1% to 90.8%). In the discovery cohort, tumours with higher basal-like scores had fewer arrest-side cells, and TGM2 expression was modestly higher on the arrest-associated side in both cohorts. The contrast did not track cell-line drug sensitivity or survival in bulk tumours. Conclusion: Untreated PDAC cells show a reproducible transcriptional bias toward anti-apoptotic and cell-cycle-arrest programmes. Whether this bias predicts cellular responses to treatment remains to be tested.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: Quantitative live imaging reveals region-dependent medulloblastoma disseminationin the zebrafish brain
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Medulloblastoma is the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor, and relapse is frequently driven by dissemination within the central nervous system. Yet the early dynamics of tumor spread remain difficult to resolve in vivo. Here, we orthotopically transplanted human medulloblastoma cells into larval zebrafish and followed individual xenografts by longitudinal high-resolution confocal imaging. ONS-76 showed particularly robust dissemination, with hindbrain tumors spreading into the developing cerebellum in 81.5% of larvae, more than fourfold the frequency observed for forebrain or midbrain tumors. Disseminating cells extended along brain-surface and leptomeningeal-like regions and frequently associated with cerebral vasculature. Quantitative analysis of tumor area, perimeter, compactness, convex hull area, and fractal dimension captured changes in growth and spatial complexity over time. Dasatinib reduced tumor expansion and dissemination-related features in a concentration-dependent manner, while higher doses revealed host toxicity. These findings establish a powerful in vivo model for resolving medulloblastoma dissemination and therapeutic response.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41568-0.title: Origins and heterogeneity of colorectal cancer
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41568-0.abstract: The undulating topography of the intestinal epithelium creates regionalized homeostatic niches at the base of each crypt, with each niche supporting neutrally evolving oligoclonal stem cell populations. At the crypt base, the fate of stem cell progeny is tightly regulated by intercompartmental polarized morphogenetic gradients, which converge to instruct continuous, but controlled, epithelial-cell turnover. To initiate tumorigenesis, a neoplastic clone must defy or escape such morphogenetic constraints either by outcompeting neighbouring stem cells or by establishing an ectopic stem cell population de novo. The position of the cell-of-origin within the crypt thus determines the oncogenic mechanisms required to subvert local homeostatic control. In turn, this defines the route of carcinogenesis and underpins the pervasive heterogeneity of colorectal cancers. Here, we explore the relationship between the position of the cell-of-origin on the vertical crypt axis and the cell plasticity mechanisms co-opted and corrupted to escape homeostatic control. We consider how this influences clonal dynamics at the pre-cancer stage and initiates distinct carcinogenesis pathways engendering morphologically discrete precursor lesions. Finally, we discuss how such lesions progress to molecularly heterogeneous subtypes with distinct clinicopathological features and therapeutic outcomes, and how phenotypic, rather than just genotypic, heterogeneity promotes tumour-cell adaptation, therapeutic resistance and metastasis. This Review by Sphyris et al. discusses how the cell-of-origin determines the route of colorectal carcinogenesis and how phenotypic plasticity and heterogeneity shape tumour evolution, disease recurrence, metastatic competence and response to therapy.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.title: [18F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.abstract: Accurate visualization of glioblastoma is essential for guiding biopsy, resection and radiotherapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI is routine in clinical practice, yet it can miss metabolically active tumor outside areas of blood-brain barrier disruption. In a histopathology-validated cohort with 472 tissue samples of 61 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, we show that O-(2-[¹⁸F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET ([18F]FET PET) depicts tumor tissue significantly better than contrast-enhanced MRI (CE-MRI), especially in regions that show no enhancement on MRI. [18F]FET PET achieves substantially higher sensitivity for tumor detection (91.2% vs 52.6%) and maintains high reliability in non-enhancing tissue (positive predictive value 98.3%), findings that are consistent across newly diagnosed and recurrent disease and in both cohorts undergoing either resection or biopsy. These results indicate that [18F]FET PET complements MRI by revealing MRI-occult tumor burden. Incorporating amino acid PET into routine planning may therefore improve the accuracy of tumor visualization and, ultimately, patient management. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) is standard for patients with glioblastoma, but its ability to detect metabolically active tumours cells at the infiltrative edge is limited. Here, the authors present a prospective biopsy-validated study demonstrating that ¹⁸F-FET PET imaging can detect tumour tissue beyond that detected by CE-MRI in patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Contemporaneous network analysis characterizes symptom-network topology and core symptoms in patients with a stoma after colorectal cancer surgery
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Symptoms co-occur after colorectal cancer stoma surgery, but their network roles remain unclear. This two-center cross-sectional study included 331 consecutively recruited patients. Exploratory factor analysis identified five symptom clusters: Psychological, Peristomal Skin, Energy Deficit, Digestive-Urinary System, and Pain. Apriori association-rule analysis identified weight loss, social impairment, and mucus discharge from the anus as sentinel symptoms within the Energy Deficit, Psychological, and Digestive-Urinary System clusters, respectively; these labels reflect cross-sectional association patterns rather than temporal ordering. In the EBICglasso network, decreased subjective well-being had the highest standardized Expected Influence (z = 1.25) and standardized one-step Bridge Expected Influence (z = 4.74). Complementary nodewise regression yielded R2 = 0.634 for this symptom, and the correlation-stability coefficient for Expected Influence was 0.749. Multivariable models for the core and sentinel symptom scores explained 7.8%–23.9% of the variance, indicating modest explanatory performance. These pooled findings may inform symptom assessment but may differ across postoperative phases; the mucus-discharge finding is further limited by unrecorded anatomical eligibility. Longitudinal studies should test temporal ordering and predictive utility.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Quantum-resistant blockchain-assisted federated secure cancer diagnosis framework using hierarchical window pattern cognition network
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Breast cancer is still a major cause of cancer mortality in women, and the development of efficient, reliable and explainable diagnostic systems capable of inter-hospital data sharing while maintaining privacy of data is essential. This study proposes a Hierarchical Window Pattern Cognition Network for breast cancer diagnosis using the Breast Histopathology Images (IDC Regular Patches) dataset. The workflow starts with data collection, then the Patient-Level Data Partitioning process by applying patient identifiers to avoid training-testing overlap. The framework uses CLAHE and data augmentation, image normalization and image resizing to enhance the image consistency. The network learns hierarchical histological and cellular morphological patterns by the modules: Global Histological Representation, Cellular Morphology Learning, Adaptive Tissue Fusion and Diagnostic Probability Estimation. A federated learning framework with five clients uses Federated Averaging (FedAvg) to aggregate models and share model updates securely. The security layer uses an AES-256-GCM encryption algorithm, a SHA3-512 hashing algorithm, and a mechanism simulating those of CRYSTALS-Kyber and CRYSTALS-Dilithium for cryptographic security. Record-integrity verification is supported by a local hash-chain audit log, and predictions of the model are explained with visual and feature-level explanations by using GradCAM + + and SHAP. The proposed centralized model achieved an accuracy of 94.23%, precision of 94.00%, recall of 94.47%, F1-score of 94.24%, and ROC-AUC of 0.9651. These findings highlight the promise of combining the histopathology classification, privacy-preserving federated learning, cryptographic protection, tamper-evident audit logging and explainable artificial intelligence within a unified diagnostic framework.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Hidden baseline heterogeneity can mask treatment effects in randomized xenograft studies
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Randomization and standardized analytical workflows are central to preclinical oncology, yet they do not necessarily ensure biological comparability at baseline. Using a real-world xenograft efficacy dataset generated under standard CRO conditions, we show that biologically meaningful treatment effects can remain statistically undetected when baseline heterogeneity is not explicitly considered. Although treatment groups appeared balanced at study entry by conventional summaries, baseline tumour volume exhibited latent structure within the cohort. Pooled group-level analyses reported no significant treatment effect, whereas baseline-aware evaluation of tumour growth trajectories revealed a responder subpopulation whose signal was masked by aggregation. This discrepancy did not arise from deficiencies in experimental conduct or data quality, but from limitations of pooled inference in the presence of structured baseline variability. Extending this framework to publicly available xenograft datasets, we observed that baseline tumour volume heterogeneity is common under routine preclinical workflows and can similarly alter efficacy interpretation. Together, these findings indicate that baseline tumour burden represents a biologically consequential source of hidden heterogeneity and that baseline-aware analytical strategies can improve the sensitivity and interpretability of preclinical efficacy assessment without deviation from standard experimental practice.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Design and characterization of beta-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 to enhance luteolin solubility and anticancer efficacy: bioinformatic and biologic assessment
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a cause of cancer-related mortality, while luteolin, a flavonoid, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, and low bioavailability. This study developed a luteolin-loaded β-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8) nanocarrier intended to improve drug retention, pH-responsive release, and anticancer activity against colorectal cancer cells. ZIF-8 nanoparticles were synthesized by room-temperature precipitation, coated sequentially with β-cyclodextrin and chitosan, crosslinked using sodium tripolyphosphate, and loaded with luteolin by post-synthetic incubation. Molecular docking using MOE 2024 investigated luteolin interactions with KRAS (PDB 6MBU), chitosan-binding protein (4ZXE), and VEGF (2VPF), with 5-fluorouracil as a computational comparator. FTIR, dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, pH-dependent surface-charge measurements, and FESEM characterized the formulation. Encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were quantified spectrophotometrically; release was assessed by dialysis at pH 7.4, 6.5, and 5.5. HCT116 colorectal carcinoma and normal human dermal fibroblasts underwent MTT testing. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, AO/EB microscopy, SOD activity, FRAP, and qRT-PCR for CASP3, SOD1, and IL6 evaluated cell-death and stress responses. The particles showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 228.95 ± 2.7 nm, a PDI of 0.139 ± 0.04, and a zeta potential of − 27.24 ± 0.32 mV, indicating a uniform nanoscale dispersion. Synthesis yield was 78.5 ± 3.2%. Measured luteolin retention increased with feed concentration, reaching 83.5 ± 1.44% encapsulation efficiency and 16.1 ± 1.53% loading capacity. Release was slower under physiological conditions and accelerated in acidic media, supporting pH-responsive behavior; model fitting was descriptive, with Higuchi favored at pH 7.4, Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 6.5, and the lowest AIC assigned to Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 5.5. In HCT116, free luteolin produced an IC50 of 166.5 ± 12.3 µg/mL, whereas Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8 reduced the IC50 to 45.96 ± 2.3 µg/mL (approximately 3.6-fold greater potency; p < 0.001). The formulation IC50 in HDF cells was 128.7 ± 8.4 µg/mL, yielding an HCT116/HDF selectivity index of 2.8. At 66 µg/mL, total apoptosis reached 48.9 ± 2.9%, compared with 1.3 ± 0.3% in controls. FRAP antioxidant capacity decreased to 0.578 ± 0.015 versus 0.801 ± 0.022 in controls. CASP3 and SOD1 transcripts increased 4.98-fold and 4.10-fold, respectively, while IL6 peaked at 10.92-fold at the intermediate dose. The dual-coated nanocarrier enhanced luteolin potency and apoptosis-associated responses in HCT116, with selectivity relative to HDF cells. Docking and characterization findings are supportive, not proof of KRAS inhibition, tumor targeting, or in vivo efficacy; validation remains necessary.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal a senescence-associated lipid-metabolic macrophage phenotype driving immunosuppression and poor prognosis in colorectal cancer
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their functional heterogeneity remains poorly understood, especially regarding the interplay between cellular senescence and lipid metabolism. We integrated multi-omics and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize a novel macrophage subpopulation termed senescence-associated lipid-metabolic (SALM) macrophages. Using eight machine learning algorithms, a prognostic model based on SALM signatures was developed and internally evaluated via nested cross-validation in a combined TCGA–GSE39582 cohort. Spatial multiplex immunofluorescence and qPCR were employed for experimental validation. SALM macrophages exhibit elevated IL-10/STAT3 signaling, terminal differentiation, and a core gene module enriched in senescence and lipid metabolism pathways. They interact strongly with T cells via immunosuppressive ligands IL-10 and MIF. Spatial analysis confirmed p16+CD68+IL-10+ cell enrichment at the tumor front. The SALM-based prognostic model achieved high accuracy (AUC = 0.972), and a corresponding nomogram showed potential for personalized prognosis prediction. SALM macrophages drive immunosuppression in CRC through a senescence-lipid metabolism axis, serving as a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Expression patterns of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p in a murine model of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: SLC38A4 (SNAT4), a system A amino acid transporter, contributes to nutrient uptake and metabolic regulation, but its role in the progression of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is unclear. We examined the expression of Slc38a4 and its predicted regulatory miRNA, mmu-miR-6948-3p, in primary tumors, invasive mammary tumors, and lung metastases in a murine TNBC model. RNA-sequencing data (GSE150928) from primary mammary tumors and lung metastases were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by functional enrichment, protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and miRNA–mRNA target prediction. Eighteen female BALB/c mice implanted with 4T1 TNBC cells were grouped into those with primary mammary tumors and those with lung metastases. Expression of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p was measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT–PCR). Public human datasets (TCGA, MET500, DepMap) were also examined. In the RNA-seq data, Slc38a4 was upregulated in lung metastases relative to primary tumors (logFC = 3.93) and was assigned to a PPI cluster enriched for amino acid transport and vesicle trafficking. qRT–PCR confirmed higher Slc38a4 expression in lung metastases (6.23 ± 0.48 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) and lower expression in invasive mammary tumors (0.51 ± 0.05 vs. 1.00 ± 0.08, P < 0.0001) than in primary tumors. Levels of mmu-miR-6948-3p did not differ significantly between groups. In human data, SLC38A4 mRNA was lower in breast tumors than in normal breast tissue, and DNA methylation showed no clear relationship with its expression. Slc38a4 expression depends on tissue context during TNBC progression, being lower in invasive mammary tumors and higher in lung metastases, and this pattern is not explained by changes in mmu-miR-6948-3p. Functional studies are needed to determine whether the increase in the lung drives colonization or is an adaptive response to it.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41523-0.title: First-line CDK4/6 inhibitors in HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer with chronic kidney disease stage 3b–5: a target trial emulation
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41523-0.abstract: Pivotal CDK4/6 inhibitor trials in HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer defined renal eligibility by serum creatinine, excluding all patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 4–5; no head-to-head data exist. Within the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we emulated three target trials as pairwise propensity-score-matched comparisons (1134/545/520 per arm) of women with CKD stage 3b–5 initiating first-line therapy. Co-primary outcomes were 2-year composite treatment failure and all-cause mortality. Compared with palbociclib, abemaciclib and ribociclib were each associated with lower treatment failure (hazard ratio: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.68–0.90; and 0.75, 0.60–0.94) and lower mortality (0.84, 0.71–0.99; and 0.69, 0.52–0.92); ribociclib and abemaciclib did not differ. Treatment-failure associations held in all sensitivity cohorts; mortality associations did not (E-value for the confidence-interval bound, 1.11). Drug-specific safety signatures from pivotal trials were preserved. Acute kidney injury hazard was stable for abemaciclib (interaction p = 0.081) but fell for ribociclib versus palbociclib (hazard ratio from 1.29 to 0.75; interaction p = 0.012). Mapping onto a published single-cell kidney atlas places the renal transporters these agents inhibit at the site of creatinine secretion. These exploratory, unregistered analyses lack familywise error control, but the toxicity profiles may inform drug selection in advanced CKD; an isolated creatinine rise on abemaciclib may warrant cystatin C measurement before discontinuation.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41420-0.title: Hypoxia-induced circUBR5 and exosomal circUBR5 promotes ovarian cancer progression by miR-17-3p/YAP1/CTGF
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41420-0.abstract: A key trait of solid tumors is their hypoxic microenvironment, which strongly influences the course of tumor development. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) exhibit high structural stability compared to linear RNAs and function as key modulators in diverse carcinomas. Nevertheless, the interaction between these factors and hypoxia in ovarian cancer (OC) is still poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that circUBR5 contributes not only to OC pathogenesis but also to shaping the hypoxic tumor microenvironment. By integrating circRNA microarray profiling of OC cells and their secreted exosomes (EXO) with analysis of GEO datasets, we identified circUBR5 as hypoxia-responsive. Both cell-based and animal assays demonstrated that it acts as an oncogene. Mechanistic investigations employing dual-luciferase reporter experiments showed that circUBR5 directly sponges miR-17-3p, thereby de-repressing the downstream effectors YAP1 and CTGF. Hypoxia significantly upregulated circUBR5 expression in both OC cells and EXO. Functionally, knockdown of circUBR5 led to decreased proliferation of OC cells, increased apoptosis, and impaired endothelial cell-driven angiogenesis. Consistently, in vivo circUBR5 silencing attenuated tumor progression and blood vessel formation in OC xenografts. Our data elucidate a hypoxia-driven axis wherein exosomal circUBR5 promotes OC progression and tumor-endothelial crosstalk via the miR-17-3p/YAP1/CTGF signaling cascade. This study demonstrates the hypoxia/circUBR5/miR-17-3p/YAP1/CTGF axis as a critical regulator of OC malignancy and shows that circUBR5 is a promising therapeutic target.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: NeuroFusionNet: an integrated Swin Transformer and CNN–RNN framework
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: This paper proposes a novel multimodal deep learning architecture to address the challenging task of brain tumor segmentation and classification from MRI images. The model combines the strengths of Swin Transformer, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to achieve strong segmentation and classification performance. Using the three-dimensional and sequential features of MRI images, the model provides comprehensive and precise brain tumor analysis. The framework consists of two primary segments: Swin Transformer and CNN-RNN. The Swin Transformer module extracts spatial features from MRI images by using a hierarchical approach to capture multi-scale features. This module provides a strong representation of tumor spatial features, which is crucial for precise segmentation and classification. The CNN-RNN module captures sequential relationships present in MRI images. The module leverages the CNN-RNN integration to capture progressive correlations between images. By combining the spatial features extracted by the Swin Transformer module with the sequential features captured by the CNN-RNN module, the framework provides a complete representation of brain tumors. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 85.6% compared with other existing deep learning models. The proposed model also achieved an F1 score of 85%, which is also superior to other existing models. It uses the BraTS 2023 dataset for multimodal brain tumor segmentation and classification, with pixel intensity values from 0 to 255, and employs an 80/10/10 training-validation-testing split. The framework’s ability to accurately segment and classify brain tumors in clinical MRI images could help clinicians diagnose and treat brain tumors more effectively. Medical practitioners can use our proposed approach to quickly correlate patients’ MRI details to analyse tumor presence. Moreover, the framework’s modular design allows easy implementation across other medical imaging tasks, making it a valuable resource for evaluating medical images.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: An optimized convolutional dense network for skin cancer detection in dermatological diagnostics
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Early skin cancer detection is essential because it improves survival rates, enables timely and less invasive treatment, reduces healthcare costs, prevents disease progression, and increases public awareness, ultimately promoting better long-term health and more effective preventive care strategies. However, prevailing approaches face challenges, namely high false-positive rates, overfitting, and reduced accuracy. This work presents a novel approach named convolutional dense network-caracal narwhal optimization algorithm (CDen-Net), for skin cancer detection leveraging input skin images. The process starts by retrieving the skin image selected from the available dataset, followed by pre-processing with a sharpening filter. Next, the skin lesion is segmented employing an adaptive dual-stream hybrid encoder and focal attention decoder network, where the loss functions are adjusted with the proposed focal-cosh loss. Image augmentation is then performed on the segmented images using region cropping, color jittering, and dihedral transformation. Various features are extracted from the augmented images, and diagnosis of skin cancer is carried out utilizing the convolutional dense network (Conv-DenNet). Finally, the network's parameters are fine-tuned for optimal performance using the proposed caracal narwhal optimization algorithm. Furthermore, the developed CDen-Net achieved a false positive rate of 4.532%, an accuracy of 96.382%, and a true positive rate of 97.592%.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41419-0.title: Targeting mutant p53 aggregates in pancreatic cancer using an autophagy-targeting chimera
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41419-0.abstract: Protein aggregation is increasingly recognized as a fundamental feature of cancer biology, particularly in tumors experiencing chronic proteotoxic stress. TP53 is one of the most frequently mutated genes in human cancers, and many cancer-associated missense mutations promote p53 misfolding and amyloid-like aggregation. These aggregates impair wild-type tumor-suppressive functions while conferring oncogenic gain-of-function (GOF) activities that promote tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Despite decades of effort, direct pharmacological targeting of mutant p53 has remained challenging because of its structural properties, including the lack of a readily druggable pocket, as well as its extensive mutational heterogeneity. Here, we employed the AUTOTAC platform to target mutant p53 aggregates by exploiting aggregation-associated conformational features characteristic of β-sheet-rich oligomers and protofibrillar aggregates. ATC-37 was designed by linking a methylene blue-derived amyloid-binding ligand, which preferentially recognizes β-sheet-rich protein aggregates, to an autophagy-targeting ligand (ATL) that allosterically activates the autophagy receptor p62/SQSTM1. This design enables engagement of amyloid-like mutant p53 aggregates and promotes their recruitment to autophagosomes. ATC-37 exhibits a dual, concentration-dependent mechanism of action. At low concentrations, it promotes autophagic degradation of mutant p53 aggregates and suppresses downstream GOF signaling. At higher concentrations, it induces p62-dependent sequestration of mutant p53 aggregates that exceeds autophagic capacity, leading to proteotoxic cell death. In a PANC-1 pancreatic cancer xenograft model, ATC-37 significantly inhibited tumor growth, reduced amyloid-like mutant p53 aggregates, and attenuated mutant p53-associated GOF programs. Importantly, ATC-37 also enhanced the response of mutant p53 pancreatic cancer cells to radiation, suggesting potential utility in combination with radiotherapy. These findings establish aggregation-state-directed AUTOTAC therapy as a conceptually innovative, mutation-agnostic strategy for targeting aggregation-prone mutant p53 and potentially other aggregation-prone oncoproteins.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Dietary diversity score, alternative healthy eating index and odds of breast cancer
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Previous studies have mainly focused on individual food groups and nutrients in relation to breast cancer and few studies have considered diet as a whole variable. The aim of this study was to examine the association of dietary diversity score (DDS) and alternative healthy eating index-2010 (AHEI-2010) with odds of breast cancer. In this case-control study, we enrolled 477 pathologically confirmed cases of breast cancer and 506 age-matched controls. Dietary assessment was done using a food frequency questionnaire. Dietary indices including DDS and AHEI-2010 were constructed according to standard methods. After controlling for potential confounders, we found a significant inverse association between DDS and odds of breast cancer; individuals in the highest tertile of DDS had 37% lower odds for having breast cancer compared with those in the lowest tertile (OR: 0.63, 95% CI: 0.42–0.95). Such a significant inverse association was also seen among post-menopausal women; such that after taking potential confounders into account, women in the top tertile of DDS score were 60% less likely to have breast cancer compared with those in the bottom tertile (OR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19–0.83). With regard to AHEI, we found no significant association between AHEI score and odds of breast cancer either before or after controlling for potential confounders. This association remained non-significant either in pre-menopausal or post-menopausal women. We found that adherence to a diet with high diversity was associated with decreased odds of breast cancer. However, no significant association was observed between AHEI and breast cancer.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s44303-0.title: CD3ε F(ab’)₂ PET imaging captures systemic and intratumoral T-cell response to immune checkpoint blockade
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44303-0.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet only a subset of patients achieve durable responses. Because the spatial distribution of T cells within tumors and lymphoid tissues shapes therapeutic outcomes, noninvasive methods capable of monitoring these populations could improve the evaluation of antitumor immune responses. Here, we report the validation of a CD3ε-targeted F(ab’)2 positron emission tomography (PET) probe for noninvasive mapping of T-lymphocytes across tumors and lymphoid tissues and characterize its effects on endogenous T-cell biology. Relative to the full-length IgG construct, the F(ab’)2 format demonstrated more rapid blood clearance, enabled high-contrast imaging within 24 h, produced limited changes in endogenous T-cell populations, and did not measurably impair T-cell activation at imaging-relevant concentrations. CD3ε F(ab’)2 PET detected tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and lymphocytes within the tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLN) across multiple syngeneic tumor models and in a genetically engineered mouse model of lung adenocarcinoma. In a combination immunotherapy study, tumor uptake distinguished responding from non-responding lesions and detected treatment-associated changes across peripheral lymphoid tissues. These results support CD3ε F(ab’)2 PET as a noninvasive imaging approach that enables assessment of T-cell distribution during tumor growth and therapy, with potential applications in mechanistic studies, biomarker development, and preclinical evaluation of immunomodulatory therapies.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: A consensus-based interpretable machine learning framework for robust early diagnosis of ovarian cancer using hematological and tumor biomarkers
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: The early and accurate diagnosis of any type of ovarian cancer is one of the key clinical issues because of the heterogeneous expression of biomarkers and the high prices of false-negative diagnosis. The proposed study is a consensus-based machine learning framework that can improve diagnostic stability, interpretability and clinical utility by utilizing routine hematological and tumor marker data. They experimentally tested 15 machine learning classifiers, under three feature selection paradigms: Stability Selection, BorutaSHAP, and a new Consensus Feature Selection paradigm that combines filter and wrapper feature selection. Stratified five-fold cross-validation and independent test set were used to determine its model performance and the measurement scales such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, ROC-AUC, calibration, and analysis of decision curve. A Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) Classifier using Consensus Feature Selection gave the strongest performance, with 97.14% accuracy (95% CI 90.17–99.21%), 100.00% sensitivity (95% CI 90.36–100%), and 94.12% specificity (95% CI 80.91–98.37%), with no false-negative examples among all configurations. Clinical reliability was also established on the basis of probability calibration (Brier score = 0.088), decision curve analysis with better net benefit at clinically relevant thresholds, and robustness to Gaussian noise perturbations up to 20%. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were employed to guarantee model interpretability with the most significant role of HE4, CA125 and menopausal status as shown in the existing clinical knowledge. The proposed pipeline, while constrained by sample size and single-center data, demonstrates strong proof-of-concept performance and may inform future clinical decision support and precision oncology processes, pending prospective multi-center validation.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.title: Phosphorylation-driven targeted protein degradation of oncogenic β-catenin
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-0.abstract: Therapeutic strategies to inhibit the Wnt signaling pathway for cancer treatment have, so far, failed to advance to the clinic. Induced-proximity drugs are revolutionizing our ability to tackle targets previously considered undruggable. Here, we use an unbiased genome-scale approach to identify induced-proximity protein candidates that inhibit the central Wnt signaling effector β-catenin in colorectal cancer cells. While the identification of several E3 ubiquitin ligases validates our approach, we uncover that inducing proximity to members of the Casein kinase I (CSNK1) family leads to β-catenin degradation and inhibits the growth of colorectal cancer cells harboring Wnt pathway mutations. We show that β-catenin degradation induced by CSNK1 proximity is kinase activity- and proteasome-dependent. We propose that the formation of a neo-degron, through kinase recruitment, can expand induced-proximity drug targeting strategies. Wolf et al. used proteome-scale induced-proximity screens for inhibitors of the oncogene β-catenin in colorectal cancer and discovered induced kinase-dependent degradation as an expansion of the Targeted Protein Degradation concept.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Safety assessment of a novel cold atmospheric pressure plasma multijet device for biomedical applications
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma (CAP) is gaining attention in medicine for its antimicrobial and pro-proliferative effects in wound healing, and is emerging as a promising oncological therapy with high efficacy and minimal side effects. Current CAP technologies face distinct limitations on biological surfaces. Dielectric barrier discharge devices are difficult to apply to non-uniform surfaces due to variable electrode distance, while single-outlet plasma jets, though more suitable for irregular geometries, provide limited coverage and require prolonged treatment times. This study presents a safety assessment of a novel multijet CAP device, conducted in accordance with DIN SPEC 91315:2025-07. The helium-based system demonstrates consistent, treatment time-dependent surface coverage and low liquid evaporation, attributable to its low gas flow. Ex vivo, contactless temperature measurements showed that continuous manual treatment does not increase surface temperature beyond 40 °C. Electrical characterisation revealed a stable, controlled power profile modulated by input voltage and treatment distance. In vitro genotoxicity testing showed no chromosomal damage in HaCaT keratinocytes. Prolonged continuous exposure in confluent cultures caused minimal cytotoxicity, suggesting good tolerance up to three minutes at the 70% threshold. Overall, these findings demonstrate a safe, controllable plasma delivery platform for biological applications, supporting further development toward clinical translation.

https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.title: The methionine cycle sustains the mesenchymal phenotype of tumor cells and drives PDA progression
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898.abstract: Mesenchymal traits are associated with poor prognosis in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDA), but direct targeting of mesenchymal tumor cells remains a challenge. Metabolic profiling of tumor cells isolated from murine PDA and liver metastases (LM) revealed that LM rely more on the methionine cycle than does primary PDA. This metabolic shift was specifically associated with increased activation of the methionine cycle in mesenchymal tumor cells compared to differentiated tumor cells. We show that the targeting of the key enzyme of the methionine cycle S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase (SAHH) in mesenchymal cells lowers the levels of homocysteine (Hcy) and glutathione, resulting in reduced antioxidant capacity, deregulated intracellular calcium homeostasis, and ultimately loss of mesenchymal markers. Together, these events decrease cell proliferation and invasion, blunting the tumorigenic and metastatic potential of SAHH-deficient cells, eventually impeding tumor growth and progression of the metastatic disease. Clinically, the high expression of SAHH in patients with mesenchymal PDA is correlated with poor survival, positioning SAHH as a potential therapeutic target to impede the pro-metastatic, mesenchymal phenotype of PDA.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41540-0.title: Discrete viscoelastic model of deformable immune cell migration through confined tumor microchannels
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41540-0.abstract: Understanding the mechanical behavior of immune cells as they migrate through the complex environment of solid tumors may be crucial for improving immunotherapy strategies. In this work, we present a particle-based model that captures the large deformations of single immune cells migrating through confined microchannels, which mimic the narrow tumor micropores. In our model, the nucleus, the cytoplasm, and the outer cell boundary are represented through discrete particles with different interacting forces that account for the differences in the mechanical properties of the discrete parts of the cell. We compare and validate the model with experimental measurements from microfluidic devices, providing relevant mechanistic insights into the effects of changes in cellular stiffness on migration efficiency.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Computational discovery of lead natural compounds targeting the HPV16 E6–E6AP–p53 interaction
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: Human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) contributes to malignant progression by recruiting host E6-associated protein (E6AP), which facilitates ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the tumor suppressor protein p53.This study employed an integrated computational strategy to screen natural compounds for their potential to bind HPV16 E6 binding pocket and disrupt​ its interaction with the E6AP, thereby potentially preserving p53 function. The HPV16 E6–E6AP–p53 complex (PDB ID: 4XR8) was retrieved, assessed for structural quality, and analyzed for binding pocket identification. GO and KEGG were performed to explore associated biological functions and pathways. Pharmacophore-based virtual screening and molecular docking were conducted to screen high-affinity compounds, followed by ADMET, toxicity prediction, density functional theory (DFT) analysis, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation. Finally, protein–ligand interactions were analyzed to characterize key binding residues. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that the E6–E6AP–p53 gene set is associated with apoptosis, DNA damage response, and viral carcinogenesis pathways. Structural validation showed acceptable stereochemical and structural quality metrics. Pharmacophore-based screening of ​511 natural compounds followed by molecular docking identified several molecules with favorable binding affinities (−​11.0 to −​11.7 kcal/mol). The six top-ranked compounds were then filtered by ADME and toxicity predictions, and C-12 and C-17 were prioritized because they combined high docking affinity (−​11.4 kcal/mol) with acceptable pharmacokinetic properties and safety profiles. Interaction analysis confirmed stable binding within the E6–E6AP–p53 pocket. DFT calculations revealed that C-17 exhibited the smallest HOMO–LUMO energy gap compared with the luteolin and C-12, indicating a distinct electronic profile. Molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA analyses indicated greater stability and a more favorable binding free energy for C-17, followed by C-12, over the reference inhibitor, luteolin. Overall, C-12 and C-17 emerged as promising candidates for inhibiting the E6–E6AP–p53 interaction, which may help restore p53 function in HPV-driven tumor biology, and warrant further experimental validation.

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.title: Prognostic role of 18FDG-PET/CT based biomarker, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer survival
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-0.abstract: To determine prognostic strength of 18FDG PET/CT based glucose metabolism, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer (BC) patients. The cohort study conducted at PET/CT Section of one of the tertiary care hospitals in Karachi, Pakistan. A total of 110 patients with advanced-stage breast cancer (predominantly stage II or higher) who underwent baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT between April 2017 and July 2020 were included. Patients were followed for up to five years from date of baseline 18FDG PET/CT, and metabolic progression-free survival (mPFS) was assessed using serial 18FDG PET/CT findings. Tumor demographics (type, grading, staging) and immunohistochemistry (estrogen receptor ER, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 HER2/Neu, progesterone receptor PR, Ki-67) were also recorded. Using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis, the significant predictors of complete metabolic response (CMR) based on binary outcome (CMR achieved and not achieved) were analyzed. Kaplan Meier’s survival plots were analyzed to measure mPFS against ROC derived cutoff values of significant predictors. The median age of study group was 57 years (25–86 years), significantly obese and 85% invasive ductal CA with 97% grade II-III on Bloom-Richardson classification and stage IV disease (74%). The significant association of maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and Ki-67 index were found in CMR on logistic regression while no significant association of patients’ age, BMI, tumor grading, ER, PR, HER-2/neu status were found in CMR in BC. SUVmax > 5.4 and Ki-67 > 30% were found to have significant association with failure to achieve CMR (AUC 0.729 and 0.759; p = 0.0002* and p = 0.0001* respectively). The mPFS was significantly shorter in patients with SUVmax > 5.4 (29 vs. 45 months; Logrank = 16.356; p = 0.0001*) and in patients with Ki-67 > 30% index (27 vs. 48 months; Logrank = 14.901; p = 0.0001*). Higher baseline SUVmax (> 5.4) and Ki-67 index (> 30%) on baseline 18FDG were associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CMR and significantly shorter mPFS in breast cancer patients. Integration of metabolic and proliferative biomarkers may improve prognostic risk stratification, particularly in advanced breast cancer.
